name: jobs
description: Lists jobs started from the current shell session and their state (running/stopped).

flags.description: Job specifier used by fg/bg/kill, e.g. fg %1.

examples.explanation: The & launches the command in the background; the shell prints the job number and PID.
Ctrl+Z suspends the foreground job; bg resumes it in the background. fg %1 brings it back to the foreground.

about: Job control is a shell feature (bash/zsh). Background jobs keep running as long as the shell lives; when the terminal closes, they receive SIGHUP — unless started with nohup or disowned. Background jobs attached to the terminal still write to it; redirect their output for clean logs.
useCases: Suspend an editor, run a quick command, resume with fg.
Run long tasks in the background.
Manage multiple concurrent tasks in one terminal.
mistakes: Closing the terminal and losing background jobs — use nohup or disown for persistence.
